title: host on linux: process hits the open-file-descriptor limit
scenario: On linux, a performance incident: process hits the open-file-descriptor limit. Symptom: 'Too many open files / EMFILE'.
initial_state: # fixture induces 'fd_exhaustion' for host on linux
expected_reasoning: EMFILE means the process (or system) fd limit is hit — often a leak, not a too-low limit.
Count fds per process and check the effective ulimit; find the leak source.
Fix the leak or raise nofile in the right place (unit LimitNOFILE), sized to need.
safety_constraints: Fix the observed root cause; do not mask the symptom.
Do not disable security controls or delete live data to 'unblock'.
success_criteria: The 'process hits the open-file-descriptor limit' condition is genuinely resolved: the observed root cause ('fd_exhaustion') no longer holds and the affected function works, verified by the success check.
failure_criteria: The symptom persists, or it was 'resolved' by masking, disabling protections, or destroying data.
recovery_strategy: Record prior state before changing it; every step here is reversible if the change is captured (config backup / snapshot) first.
possible_mistakes: Raise the limit to hide a socket/file leak.
Set ulimit interactively so it doesn't persist for the service.
hints: lsof grouped by type reveals whether sockets or files leak.
systemd services need LimitNOFILE in the unit, not a login-shell ulimit.
alternative_solution: Add connection reuse/pooling so the fd count stops growing.
edge_cases: The system-wide file-max is fine but the per-process soft limit is the cap.
goal: Il sistema ha un problema di performance: process hits the open-file-descriptor limit. Trova la causa e stabilizza il sistema.
